speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to examine the skin lesions you are concerned about; please describe their appearance, location, and how long they have been present. To begin our assessment, can you tell me if these spots are changing in size, shape, or color, or if you are experiencing any pain or bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. Given your age, significant smoking history, and the location of these non-healing, crusty lesions, I am concerned about potential malignancy. Can you tell me if you have noticed any swelling, ulceration, or difficulty urinating related to the penile lesion, and when exactly you first noticed these spots?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Acral/Hand).

The clinical picture of non-healing, painless, crusty lesions in a 62-year-old heavy smoker, specifically involving the penis and the middle finger (a site for subungual/acral SCC), strongly points to this diagnosis. Please confirm if you have any history of chronic hand infections or arsenic exposure, and if you are currently on immunosuppressive therapy.
